metadata.name: National Bank of Kuwait (NBK)
metadata.provenance: financials built 25-Nov-26 from NBK FY2025 Audited & 9M 2026 Interim Financial Statements (Boursa Kuwait / IR, Nov-26); quotes await [BBG]

financials_multi_year.source: NBK FY2025 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements (Boursa Kuwait / IR), read 25-Nov-26

observations.notes: FY25 assets KWD 45.6bn ($149.4bn, +13.1% YoY), net operating income KWD 1.3bn, NPAT KWD 575.6m, NPL 1.36% (240% coverage), CAR 17.0%.

9M26 assets KWD 46.9bn ($152.4bn), loans KWD 28.2bn (+8.2% YoY), deposits KWD 27.9bn (+13.5%), conventional NII KWD 587m + Islamic financing KWD 167m = KWD 754m (operating income KWD 1.0bn), NPAT KWD 481.7m (+3.1% YoY), CET1 12.8%, Tier 1 13.8%, CAR 15.9%, NPL 1.29% (236% coverage).

verdict.stance: Neutral / Premier Kuwaiti D-SIB with Fortress Asset Quality (A1 / A+ / A+)
verdict.summary: NBK delivered steady 9M26 net profit of KWD 481.7m (+3.1% YoY) on KWD 46.9bn ($152.4bn) assets, with NPLs tightening further to 1.29% (236% coverage) and deposits growing 13.5% YoY. CET1 at 12.8% and CAR at 15.9% provide solid buffers alongside sovereign D-SIB support.

positives: Kuwait's largest commercial bank (A1/A+/A+) with Boubyan Bank Islamic franchise.
Exceptional asset quality: NPL ratio 1.29% with 236% provision coverage at 9M26.
Strong deposit growth (+13.5% YoY to KWD 27.9bn) keeping LDR near 101%.
negatives: CAR moderated from 17.0% (YE25) to 15.9% (Sep-26) on 8.2% loan expansion.
Regional Kuwait/GCC sovereign fiscal and oil-cycle concentration.
Direct linkage to Kuwait sovereign credit ceiling, local policy rate cycles, and FX volatility.

background.business_overview: Flagship Kuwaiti conventional and Islamic banking group.
background.asset_perimeter: Corporate, retail, wealth management, and Boubyan Bank (Islamic subsidiary) across Kuwait, GCC, Egypt, and UK.
background.ownership_governance: Boursa Kuwait listed (NBK); systemic D-SIB with Kuwait Investment Authority backing.

recent_drivers: Nov-26 (9M26): NPAT KWD 481.7m (+3.1%), assets KWD 46.9bn, CET1 12.8%, CAR 15.9%, NPL 1.29% (236% coverage).
